Principle: A State-Change Detector Must Not Keep Its Previous-Value Memory on the Side the State Change Resets
Principle: A Diagnostic That Only Fires on a Hotkey or Only at Info Level Does Not Exist for a User Who Cannot Reach It
Principle: Never Open a File You Don't Own With a Truncating Write Mode; Never Infer Ownership of the Remainder From a Start Marker
Principle: A Derived/Instrumented Value Is Not Ground Truth When the Derivation Itself Is the Suspect Under Test
Principle: Runtime Value/Existence Claims Derived From Static RE Must Be Validated With a Live Probe Before Shipping as Verified
Principle: A Config Write Is Not Applied Until You Can Read It Back From the System That Actually Consumes It
Principle: Never Pause a Live Real-Time/VR Process With a Breakpoint Debugger; Use Non-Pausing Instrumentation Instead
Principle: Verify Build Identity (Version and Build Time) Before Believing a Fix Landed or Failed
Principle: Check Cheap Environmental Causes (Display Settings, Profile State, Runtime Config) Before a Multi-Session Code Bisect
Principle: When One of Several Similar Implementations Is Broken, Diff It Against Its Working Siblings Instead of Re-Theorizing From Scratch
Principle: Logging/Instrumentation Volume Is Not Neutral - It Can Change the Timing or Behavior Being Measured
Principle: Per-Axis Scalar Euler/Sign Compensation Cannot Fix a Wrong Rotation Frame - Diagnose and Fix the Frame Itself
Principle: A File Format Can Be Structurally/Parser-Clean Yet Semantically Unsafe at Runtime - Structural Validators Don't Model Semantic Invariants
Principle: An API Success Return (ok=1, a Flag Accepted, override=1) Proves the Call Didn't Throw, Not That It Had the Intended Effect
Principle: A Package/Mod Being Present, Deployed, or Listed Is Not Proof That Its Code Actually Loaded and Ran
